record.summary: India's national AI governance framework. It sets seven guiding principles or sutras (trust, people first, innovation over restraint, fairness and equity, accountability, understandable by design, and safety, resilience and sustainability) and recommendations across six pillars, including an India-specific risk assessment framework based on evidence of harm, a graded liability system, voluntary measures backed by techno-legal solutions, a national AI incident database, and new bodies: an AI Governance Group, a Technology & Policy Expert Committee and the AI Safety Institute. It finds that existing laws can address many risks and that a separate AI law is not needed at this stage.
record.notes: A drafting committee constituted by MeitY in July 2025 and chaired by Prof. Balaraman Ravindran (IIT Madras) wrote the guidelines. It built on a draft report by a sub-committee on AI governance under the Principal Scientific Adviser's advisory group, which MeitY published for public feedback and which drew more than 2,500 submissions; that draft is superseded by these guidelines. The seven sutras are adapted from the Reserve Bank of India's FREE-AI Committee report. Principal Scientific Adviser Prof. Ajay Kumar Sood unveiled the guidelines on 5 Nov 2025, calling 'Do No Harm' the guiding principle of the framework, ahead of the India-AI Impact Summit (New Delhi, 19-20 Feb 2026). PIB published an explainer on 15 Feb 2026 for the Summit. India has no AI-specific statute.

verification.note: Recheck of 18 Oct 2026. The official_url (IndiaAI article on indiaai.gov.in) could not be stored on any attempt (robots.txt unreachable, DNS failures, then a TLS certificate that could not be verified); copies of the PIB release on digitalindia.gov.in and negd.gov.in returned HTTP 403. Stored: the PIB release of 5 Nov 2025 (PRID 2186639, pib.gov.in, the secondary_url), the guidelines document itself (static.pib.gov.in, 68 pages) and PIB's explainer of 15 Feb 2026 (static.pib.gov.in). The guidelines confirm the title, MeitY's drafting committee, the four parts, the sutras, the six pillars, the institutions, the incident database, the risk framework, the voluntary approach and the finding that a separate AI law is not needed. The guidelines carry no date; the date of 5 Nov 2025 and the unveiling rest on the PIB release, which was stored as the record's secondary source and so counts as another official source. The guidelines do not use the phrase 'Do No Harm'; it is the Principal Scientific Adviser's description at the launch, so it moved from the summary to the notes. The explainer of 15 Feb 2026 says the guidelines were 'releasing in AI Impact Summit 2026', which reads as a reference to the Summit rather than a second release.

status.quote: India adopts a principle-based AI governance framework anchored in seven Sutras to enable safe, trusted, and inclusive AI innovation across sectors.
After extensive research, deliberations, and a review of public feedback, the Committee presents this governance framework in four parts:

legal_force.quote: Encourage compliance through voluntary measures supported by techno-legal solutions as appropriate.

legal_force.locator: page 12, Overview of India's AI Governance Framework
legal_force.quote: Therefore, at this stage, a separate law to regulate AI is not needed given the current assessment of risks.

summary.quote: Develop an India-speciﬁc risk assessment framework that reﬂects real-world evidence of harm.
Adopt a graded liability system based on the function performed, level of risk, and whether due diligence was observed.
The database should be a national-level centralised system that has the ability to query and collect data from smaller, local databases in a federated manner.
An AI Governance Group (AIGG) should be set up, to be supported by a Technology & Policy Expert Committee (TPEC).

notes.quote: The subcommittee prepared a draft report which was published by MeitY for public feedback. More than 2,500 submissions were received
Seven guiding principles or sutras have been adapted from the RBI’s FREE-AI Committee report to guide the overall approach.

judgment.status_reasoning: Unveiled by MeitY on 5 Nov 2025 and presented by PIB in February 2026 as the framework India adopts; nothing stored shows them withdrawn or replaced. Voluntary guidelines: Published (non-binding, current).
